title: [Title: name the skill and the moment, e.g. 'The two weeks before the deadline']
intro: [Intro: WHO it is for (e.g. students managing a substantial assignment), WHAT skill they practise (planning / procrastination / help-seeking / time management), and the honesty line. End with: 'This is demonstration content for discussion, not personalised academic advice.' Keep IDs below; replace all bracketed text.]

nodes.title: [Opening title: the situation in a few words]
nodes.body: [Set the scene concretely: one realistic academic situation with a low-pressure start, so the tension is 'easy to postpone', not 'already a crisis'. 2-4 sentences.]

nodes.title: [Decision 1 title: the first self-management choice]
nodes.body: [State the choice point. Make both options defensible, not obviously right vs wrong. e.g. how to start a big task.]
nodes.prompt: [Optional: a pre-choice reflection, e.g. 'What usually happens when you face a task this size?' Delete this line if unused.]

choices.label: [Option 1: the more skilful habit, phrased without judgement]

nodes.title: [Consequence 1A title: short, neutral]
nodes.body: [Show the realistic payoff of option 1. Avoid praise; just let the situation improve plausibly. The task is not magically solved, the next move is clearer.]

nodes.title: [Consequence 1B title: short, neutral]
nodes.body: [Show the realistic cost of option 2 WITHOUT humiliating the learner. Make it a natural consequence (time lost, task feels bigger), not a telling-off.]

nodes.title: Pause and reflect / 1
nodes.body: [One or two sentences naming the underlying principle this decision illustrates (e.g. 'Starting is a skill, not a mood').]
nodes.prompt: [Reflection question tied to the learner's own experience, e.g. 'What made it easier or harder to begin?']

nodes.title: [Decision 2 title: a competing demand or trade-off]
nodes.body: [A new, different self-management tension (not a repeat of decision 1). e.g. protecting planned time against a social or work demand.]

nodes.title: Pause and reflect / 2
nodes.body: [Name the principle, e.g. 'Every yes to one thing is a quiet no to another'.]
nodes.prompt: [Reflection question, e.g. 'Which commitment was easiest to drop, and why?']

nodes.title: [Decision 3 title: the help-seeking or recovery choice]
nodes.body: [A third distinct tension, ideally about getting unstuck or recovering, e.g. ask for help with a precise question vs struggle on alone.]

nodes.title: Pause and reflect / 3
nodes.body: [Name the principle, e.g. 'Asking for help early is a planning decision, not an admission of failure'.]
nodes.prompt: [Reflection question, e.g. 'What stops you asking for help sooner than you do?']

nodes.title: [Ending title: frame it as the learner's own route]
nodes.body: [Debrief: connect the three decisions back to the learning goal. Emphasise that the choices, not more hours, changed the outcome. Do not score or rank the learner.]
nodes.prompt: [Transfer question: 'What is one thing you will do differently next time?']
